correctness.rationale: For either design, conditional on tagged count \(y\), \(K\) equals in law the indicator that \(y>0\) plus richness \(R_{m-y}\) of other-species samples. A common nested coupling has increments in \(\{0,1\}\). Therefore \(R_m\le1+R_{m-1}\), and \(1+R_{m-y}\le1+R_{m-1}\) for every feasible \(y\ge2\), proving all conditional tail orders. Averaging yields all monotone-score covariances. Exact analytical higher-frequency witness families prove both signs for every \(r\ge2\); independent rational enumeration checks 12,127 finite inequalities.

value.rationale: A distribution-free first-order conditional stochastic order under both finite-census rarefaction and heterogeneous iid sampling links species richness to singleton detection at every tail threshold, not merely via a single mean or selected finite profile. Every higher frequency loses universal covariance sign, furnishing a mathematically sharp boundary. It supplies an interpretable null-model diagnostic for richness and rare-species survey relationships; no unsupported estimator or field-data generalization is claimed.
